advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that exercises run_sweep's git-toplevel resolution arm (REBAR_ROOT unset, cwd anchored at the store parent) so the co-located/local topology the fix claims to cover is actually pinned.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:250: `env = os.environ.get("REBAR_ROOT")` — REBAR_ROOT arm short-circuits before the git-toplevel arm

src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:221: comment claims the git-toplevel arm reads a cwd anchored by _proc.detached_child_cwd, but no test drives that arm (REBAR_ROOT is always set, and run_sweep runs in-process rather than through spawn_detached's anchored cwd)
advisory.finding: The new relocated-store tests all set REBAR_ROOT (via _init_relocated_store, which does monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_ROOT", str(repo))) and invoke run_sweep in-process, so config.repo_root_or_none() always resolves through its REBAR_ROOT arm. The git-toplevel-of-cwd arm — the 'locally the git toplevel is read from a cwd _proc.detached_child_cwd already anchored at the canonical store's parent' path the fix's comment explicitly relies on — is never exercised by any added test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the compact_trigger.py comment: the deployed code root read via REBAR_ROOT is /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code, not /app (which is a source-only COPY with no object DB).
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:217: `os.path.dirname(tracker) equalled the code root only for a co-located checkout, so // on the deployed topology (store /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets, code /app)`
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:385: `.dockerignore excludes .git and the image is COPY . /app, so /app is a SOURCE COPY with no object database`
advisory.finding: The inline comment justifying the fix states the deployed topology is 'store /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets, code /app', but in that deployment /app is a source COPY with no object database and REBAR_ROOT is deliberately pointed at /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code — /app is precisely the root that fails. The comment misdescribes the code root of the very scenario it fixes.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness anchor to test_run_sweep_respects_a_repo_config_that_folds_nothing (assert the sweep reached compact_all_cli / select_tickets with the resolved root) before trusting the empty-snapshot absence check.
evidence: Test body: overwrite `[compact]\nthreshold = 1\nCOMPACTION_HORIZON_NS = 3600000000000`, `compact_trigger.run_sweep(str(external))`, then `assert not list((external / tid).glob("*-SNAPSHOT.json"))` — an absence-only assertion.

run_sweep swallows all failures: `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py:238` `except Exception:` / `logger.warning("compaction sweep failed; the events stay live", exc_info=True)`, and returns silently at line 213 on `if _lock.write_lock_is_busy(tracker): ... return`.

ABSENCE rationale: unlike the companion test_run_sweep_folds_by_the_repo_compact_config which asserts PRESENCE (liveness-anchored), this test has no producer-liveness anchor, so a sweep that never ran passes it trivially.
advisory.finding: test_run_sweep_respects_a_repo_config_that_folds_nothing asserts the ABSENCE of *-SNAPSHOT.json files after run_sweep with no liveness check that the sweep actually ran. run_sweep swallows every exception (`except Exception: logger.warning(...)`) and also returns silently on a lock stand-aside (`write_lock_is_busy`) or an unacquired trigger lock, so the empty-snapshot result is produced both when the repo's folds-nothing [compact] config held the sweep back AND when the sweep never executed — the oracle cannot distinguish the intended no-fold from a sweep that crashed or stood aside.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch a seam that records the sweep actually ran (e.g. spy on compact.compact_all_cli or select_tickets and assert it was invoked with repo_root==str(repo)) before the `assert not list(...glob(...))`, so the no-fold verdict cannot be satisfied by a sweep that crashed or stood aside.
